description: The Boeotarchs were the chief federal magistrates and military commanders of ancient Boeotia, particularly within the Boeotian League. Elected from the region’s constituent districts, they combined political authority with command of the league’s armies and helped coordinate the affairs of cities such as Thebes, Orchomenus, and Thespiae. The office became especially important in the 5th and 4th centuries BC, when prominent Theban leaders such as Epaminondas and Pelopidas served as Boeotarchs. Their role illustrates how Boeotia developed a strong federal system in which military leadership and regional government were closely intertwined.
